elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained 10.4: "Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I (\"Developed Software\")" — ownership stays with Vendor; the redline targets the fallback licence instead.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere; the only added operative sentence is a licence grant ("M&I hereby grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license").

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained 10.4: "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The new grant is expressly limited to "the Developed Software"; M&I's separately-owned pre-existing programs, systems and materials remain governed by 17.2, which permits use only "during the Term". No perpetual licence to embedded Vendor IP as such.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same defect: the irrevocable grant covers only Developed Software; retained 17.2 ("no rights in any software, systems, documentation ... except ... during the Term") still governs embedded M&I pre-existing IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Royalty-free wording attaches only to the Developed Software licence, not to Vendor IP embedded in it and owned under 10.4/17.2.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 17.1 retained: "Customer shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and other Confidential Information".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 17.4 as amended: "except that M&I shall use and process Customer Data solely to provide the Services", which carves Customer Data out of the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" standard.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no joint-ownership language exists in 10.4, 17.1-17.4, and the redline creates none (Vendor retains ownership; Customer receives a licence).

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Unchanged 10.4: "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "M&I hereby grants Customer a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software"; "Notwithstanding Section 17.2" defeats the retained during-the-Term limitation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "royalty-free"; no fee or further-agreement condition attached.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business" — Developed Software is the defined work-product/deliverable category in 10.4.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Same sentence expressly includes "sublicense ... for Customer's business".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 17.4 amended to add "except that M&I shall use and process Customer Data solely to provide the Services", overriding the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" use right for Customer Data; no retained clause permits Vendor distribution or independent exploitation of Customer Data (10.4's resale right is limited to Developed Software).

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted sentence in 10.4 supplies all six licence attributes (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify, sublicense) over the defined "Developed Software", and the 17.4 carve-out supplies the Customer Data processing limitation. Vendor's retained ownership of generic programs, ideas and know-how already satisfies the first fallback element.

Preferred level is not reached: ownership of paid-for work product remains with M&I under retained 10.4, there is no assignment, and the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free grant reaches only Developed Software, leaving M&I's pre-existing programs and systems subject to 17.2's "during the Term" limitation. That is acceptable because the finding targets the fallback.

Minimal: two surgical operations, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, no duplicate operative terms. The 10.4 refund/credit mechanic, M&I's right to offer Developed Software to other customers, and the favourable 17.1 ownership sentence are all retained.

Preserves intent: "Notwithstanding Section 17.2" removes what would otherwise be a contradictory retained sentence, the 17.4 carve-out is expressed as an exception rather than replacing the mutual confidentiality standard, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting nit only (not a deviation): the 17.4 insertion sits mid-sentence before "and shall instruct their employees"; consider closing it with a comma-set or a standalone sentence so the compound predicate reads cleanly. No substantive repair required.
